newsitem.title: USA: RTRS-Golf-McGann beats Webb in playoff to win LPGA's HealthSouth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Golf-McGann beats Webb in playoff to win LPGA's HealthSouth.

text.p: Michelle McGann sank a three-foot par putt on the first playoff hole on Sunday to beat defending champion Karrie Webb of Australia and win the $600,000 LPGA HealthSouth Inaugural at Lake Buena Vista.
Webb forced the playoff with a birdie on the last hole of the final round but three-putted the first playoff hole, missing a five-footer for par at the par-4 18th.
"I'm disappointed, but I made the putt on 18 to get into the playoff," said Webb, whose bold first putt on the playoff hole ran past the hole. "It's not my frame of mind to lag it up there."
The victory, the sixth of McGann's career, was worth $90,000.
"Karrie played great today," McGann, 27, said. "It was more of who was going to hang in there the longest."
McGann and Webb both finished at nine-under-par 207. Beth Daniel finished third at 211 after posting a 70.
Webb and McGann began the third round tied for the lead and both made late charges to card three-under 69s.
Webb led by one stroke with three holes to play, but McGann had birdies at the 16th and 17th holes. Webb bounced back with her birdie at 18.

It was the second consecutive second-place finish for Webb, who was runner-up to Annika Sorenstam at last week's Tournament of Champions. She won four tournaments and more than $1 million in her rookie campaign of 1996.
McGann has set some lofty goals for herself.
"A goal of mine that I hope not to be too distant is to be Rolex Player of the Year," she said. "My game is improving and feels solid. My swing is easy to fix if I'm having problems."
For Webb, the pair of runner-up results was not a worry.
"I had my share of Sundays last year," she said. "It's early and I'm happy with the two second-place finishes."
